symbol_validation.note: PDB stream age is 3; DBI age is 1 and matches the PE CodeView age. GUID and all 22 section layouts match the installed DLL.

notes: LLVM 22.1.4 full --symbols dump stopped at an unsupported APSInt constant; its complete procedure prefix was independently checked against our raw parser.
The custom parser skips unneeded symbols by their validated framed length and parses only S_GPROC32/S_LPROC32; unsupported constants do not block later method records.

findings.finding: Validated .NET Native 1.7 custom descriptor points from app IAT 0x18029f008 to the ordinary SharedLibrary.dll!$NEAT$ import. All 4,737 slots are resolved through the exact installed SharedLibrary RVA table.

Microsoft symbol server returned the SharedLibrary PDB selected by the installed PE GUID/age. GUID, DBI age and all 22 section layouts agree with the installed DLL. PDB info-stream age 3 is recorded separately from DBI/PE age 1.

Download body 0x1804bfc90 concatenates its URL, obtains and awaits a response, gets a stream via a virtual call, constructs MemoryStream, calls Stream.CopyTo, then MemoryStream.ToArray and completes its task with the byte-array result.
findings.limitation: The virtual response stream call is not named by the SharedLibrary import resolver; parent analysis supplies that type/call-chain corroboration. This proves whole-image materialization in memory before the result reaches cache code, not a live transfer.

findings.finding: Archive body 0x1804c0e20 fetches InvariantCulture and uses String.Format for its URL, awaits a response, then constructs StreamReader over the returned stream before calling app-local JSON reader/deserialization helpers.
findings.limitation: Do not label an unobserved StreamReader.ReadToEnd call: no such direct import call appears in this scoped body. App-local JSON method names require separate evidence.

findings.finding: 0x1804c0080 constructs Uri from a string and forwards it; 0x1804c00d0 reads Uri.Scheme and compares via String.op_Inequality. Async wrapper 0x1804bfe90 creates a delegate; its body uses TaskFactory<T>.FromAsyncImpl with two callback delegates.
findings.limitation: This is consistent with WebRequest/CreateHttp/GetResponseAsync architecture; do not call these HttpClient constructors or GetStreamAsync merely from their caller role.

findings.finding: Cache analysis imports resolve to Uri.Query, Path.GetFileName, String.IsNullOrEmpty, String.Equals and StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase. The comparer name establishes ordinal case-insensitive matching for callers that use this exact imported getter.

The automatic-setting default helper has an actual PDB procedure alias System::Nullable$1<System::Boolean>.GetValueOrDefault at the same byte-return routine already decoded by REA. The custom import table now confirms the zero-based NEAT mapping; prior speculative zero/one-based ambiguity is removed.
findings.limitation: Current UI settings still were not read or changed by this subtask.

limitations: The application PDB was probed once at its exact Microsoft symbol-server key and returned HTTP 404. No application source method-name map is claimed.
Compiler folding means one native address can have many unrelated method names; choose the relevant alias only with call-site argument/type evidence.
Complete aliases are retained in sharedlibrary-symbols.json; per-slot samples are capped at 64 with count/truncation flags.
The application NativeFormat RVA method table and managed catch types were not decoded; no source-code or full-C# reconstruction is claimed.
All installed target interactions were read-only. No target process, UI, settings, or network request from the application was executed.
